mainTopic: אביי and רבא on putting סכך over an אכסדרה (portico) with פצימין (posts): does פי תקרה יורד וסותם (or לבוד) create walls for the סוכה? The גמרא also gives two versions of the dispute, from סורא and from פומבדיתא.
overview: In the סורא version, everyone agrees that סכך over an אכסדרה with posts is כשרה. אביי and רבא argue about a portico without posts. אביי says the edge of the portico roof 'comes down and closes' (פי תקרה יורד וסותם), and רבא says that rule only makes walls for the portico itself. A משנה is raised against אביי, and רבא answers it for him: there the roofs were made level, so no edge shows. In the פומבדיתא version, the argument is instead about a portico with posts and whether לבוד makes walls for the סוכה. The הלכה follows the סורא version. רב אשי challenges רב כהנא for building on a portico without posts, and the answer is that it really had a post, seen from one side only, just like a לחי in a מבוי. Next comes a ברייתא: פסל that 'goes out' from the סוכה is treated like the סוכה. עולא, רבה with רב יוסף, רבי יוחנן and רבי אושעיא each explain it differently. רבי אושעיא's reading leads to the question of whether something can count toward a measure without being valid itself, and רבי יצחק בן אלישיב's answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The dispute is according to רב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says אביי and רבא both work within רב's view, and אביי simply follows רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: When they argue, it is according to רב. אביי holds like רב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how the argument between אביי and רבא fits with רב's known rule that the edge of a roof creates a wall. It is also setting up the next step, which explains how רבא can disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ruled that an אכסדרה in a field is considered enclosed because of פי תקרה יורד וסותם. אביי applies that same rule to the סוכה next to the portico. So nobody is rejecting רב. The question is only how far רב's rule reaches.

keyTerms.meaning: the edge of the roof is viewed as coming down and closing off, forming a wall
a portico, a roofed porch open on one side

steps.whyThisMatters: It changes the argument from 'whether פי תקרה exists' to 'when פי תקרה works.'

phrases.english: When they disagree, it is according to Rav.
Abaye holds like Rav,
phrases.notes: אביי applies 'the edge of the roof comes down' to the sukkah as well.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion of רב's ruling about an אכסדרה in a field.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both אביי and רבא accept רב's rule. אביי extends it to the סוכה case.

steps.title: רבא limits רב's rule to walls made for the portico
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that רב's rule only works when the roof-edge 'walls' serve the portico itself, not a סוכה outside it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא would tell you: רב only said this there because the walls serve the portico. But here, where they are not made for this purpose, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how רבא can disagree with אביי while still accepting רב's rule. He draws a line between the two cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רב's case, the roof-edge walls enclose the portico itself, the very space under that roof. In the סוכה case, those same roof edges would have to serve as walls for a different structure, the סוכה beside the portico. רבא says פי תקרה does not create walls for something it was not built for.

keyTerms.meaning: he only said his ruling up to this point (a limiting formula)

steps.whyThisMatters: It introduces a lasting idea: a halachic wall may count only for the space it was made to serve.

phrases.english: And Rava would say to you:

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא אָמַר רַב הָתָם
phrases.english: Rav only said his ruling there
because the walls are made for the portico,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הָכָא דְּלָאו לְהָכִי עֲבִידִי, לָא.
phrases.english: but here, where they are not made for this, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרָבָא אָמַר לָךְ: עַד כָּאן לָא אָמַר רַב הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the hidden question of how רבא can rule against אביי if both follow רב.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since רב holds פי תקרה, it should work for the סוכה too.
steps.terutzMaskana: פי תקרה only makes walls for the space under that roof, the portico, and not for a סוכה outside it.

steps.title: Challenge to אביי from the משנה of the courtyard surrounded by a portico
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules a סוכה in a courtyard surrounded by a portico פסולה. Why not say פי תקרה יורד וסותם, as אביי does?
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned: 'And likewise, a courtyard surrounded by a portico.' Why is it invalid? Let us say the edge of the roof comes down and closes!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה that seems to contradict אביי's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that if there are four אמות of invalid roofing (the portico roof) before the סכך begins, the סוכה is פסולה. If אביי were right, the edge of the portico roof should form a wall right where the סכך starts. Then the סוכה would have its own walls and be כשרה. This looks like proof against אביי.

phrases.english: We learned: And likewise, a courtyard surrounded by a portico.
phrases.notes: The משנה rules it invalid when four אמות of invalid roofing separate the walls from the סכך.

phrases.english: And why?
Let us say the edge of the roof comes down and closes!

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן: וְכֵן חָצֵר הַמּוּקֶּפֶת אַכְסַדְרָה. וְאַמַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests אביי's position against a משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's view that פי תקרה makes walls for a סוכה beside the portico.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If פי תקרה works for the סוכה, the משנה's case should be כשרה, yet the משנה rules it פסולה.

steps.title: רבא answers for אביי: the roofs were made level
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that the משנה deals with a case where the סכך is level with the portico roof, so no visible roof edge exists.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא explained it according to אביי: it is a case where he made its roofing level.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא, even though he disagrees with אביי, defends אביי's view against the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: פי תקרה needs a visible edge, a drop where the roof ends. If the סכך is at the same height as the portico roof, no edge can be seen from inside the סוכה. So nothing 'comes down,' and the משנה's ruling of פסולה fits אביי's view.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבא changed his mind. He is only showing that the משנה does not disprove אביי.

phrases.english: Rava explained it according to Abaye:
when he made its roofing level.
phrases.notes: The סכך is at the same height as the portico roof, so no edge is visible.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא against אביי.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה speaks of any portico, so it contradicts פי תקרה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה speaks of level roofs with no visible edge, so פי תקרה never applies there.

steps.title: The פומבדיתא version of the dispute
steps.stepSummary: סורא taught the dispute as above. פומבדיתא taught it differently: a portico without posts is פסולה for everyone, and with posts אביי says כשרה while רבא says פסולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: In סורא they taught this teaching in this wording. In פומבדיתא they taught: If one put סכך on a portico without posts, everyone agrees it is invalid. If it has posts, אביי says valid and רבא says invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second tradition of the whole argument. This step sets up the reasoning that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now we followed the סורא version. In the פומבדיתא version, the case 'without posts' is invalid for everyone. The argument is only about a portico that has posts. The reasons for each side come in the next step.

phrases.aramaic: בְּסוּרָא מַתְנִי לְהָא שְׁמַעְתָּא בְּהַאי לִישָּׁנָא.
phrases.english: In Sura they taught this teaching in this wording.
In Pumbedita they taught:

phrases.aramaic: סִיכֵּךְ עַל גַּבֵּי אַכְסַדְרָה שֶׁאֵין לָהּ פַּצִּימִין,
phrases.english: If one put schach over a portico that has no posts,
all agree it is invalid.
If it has posts,
Abaye says: valid,
Rava says: invalid.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּסוּרָא מַתְנִי לְהָא שְׁמַעְתָּא בְּהַאי לִישָּׁנָא. בְּפוּמְבְּדִיתָא מַתְנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a second tradition of the same dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Without posts, the סוכה is פסולה for everyone. With posts, אביי rules כשרה and רבא rules פסולה.

steps.title: The reasons in the פומבדיתא version: לבוד
steps.stepSummary: In the פומבדיתא version, אביי's reason is that we apply לבוד. רבא's reason is that we do not apply לבוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי says valid: we say לבוד. רבא says invalid: we do not say לבוד.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reason behind each side in the פומבדיתא version.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the argument is not about פי תקרה at all. It is about לבוד, the rule that a gap of less than three טפחים counts as closed. אביי treats the posts as joined into a wall that also counts for the סוכה. רבא does not let לבוד make a wall for the סוכה.

keyTerms.meaning: the rule that a gap of less than three טפחים is treated as joined or closed

steps.confusionAlert: Watch the switch: in סורא the issue is פי תקרה, and in פומבדיתא the issue is לבוד.

phrases.english: Abaye says valid:
we say lavud.
Rava says invalid:
we do not say lavud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning for the rulings in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In פומבדיתא, the dispute is whether לבוד makes walls for the סוכה.

steps.title: The הלכה follows the first version
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rules that the halacha follows the first version, the one from סורא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is according to the first version.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא decides between the two traditions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The סורא version, where the dispute is about פי תקרה, is the one accepted for halacha. The פומבדיתא version, which made it a dispute about לבוד, is not followed.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two versions of the אביי and רבא dispute. In סורא it is about פי תקרה, and רבא limits it to walls made for the portico. In פומבדיתא it is about לבוד. The halacha follows the first, סורא version.

phrases.english: And the halacha is like the first version.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides between the two versions of steps 1-4 and 5-6.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The halacha follows the סורא framing, where the dispute is about פי תקרה.

steps.title: רב אשי challenges רב כהנא's sukkah on a portico without posts
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי sees רב כהנא putting סכך on an אכסדרה without פצימין and challenges him from רבא's ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי found רב כהנא putting סכך on a portico that had no posts. He said to him: Don't you hold like רבא, who said that with posts it is כשרה and without posts it is פסולה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a real-life story. רב אשי sees what looks like a פסולה סוכה and challenges רב כהנא with רבא's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We just learned that the הלכה follows the סורא version, where רבא says a portico without posts is פסולה. רב כהנא seems to be acting against that ruling. So רב אשי's question is really a challenge: how can you build here?

keyTerms.meaning: a portico, a roofed area open on the sides
posts or wall-stubs that stand out and show the walls' edges
Doesn't the master hold...? (a polite challenge)

phrases.english: Rav Ashi found Rav Kahana
who was putting roofing on top of a portico
that had no posts.
He said to him: Doesn't the master hold
that which Rava said:
if it has posts, it is fit;
phrases.notes: This matches רבא's view in the סורא version, which is the הלכה.

phrases.english: if it has no posts, it is unfit!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לָא סָבַר מָר הָא דְּאָמַר רָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the ruling from step 7 (הלכה like the סורא version) to a real case.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב כהנא's practice of building a סוכה on a portico that seems to have no posts.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to רבא, whose view is accepted, a portico without פצימין is פסולה, so רב כהנא's סוכה should be פסולה.

steps.title: רב כהנא shows the post is visible from inside
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא shows that there really is a post: it sticks out on the inside but is flush on the outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: He showed him: it was visible from the inside and flush from the outside.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא answers by showing that his portico really does have a post. It just isn't visible from every side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: From outside the wall looked smooth, so it seemed there was no post. But on the inside a piece of wall stuck out. That piece counts as פצימין, so the סוכה is כשרה even according to רבא.

phrases.english: He showed him
it was visible from the inside and even on the outside.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: the portico actually has a post.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב כהנא's portico has no פצימין at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: It has a post that shows on the inside only. That is enough to count as פצימין.

steps.title: Another version: the post is visible from outside
steps.stepSummary: A second version says the post stuck out on the outside but was flush on the inside.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or else: it was visible from the outside and flush on the inside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another version of what רב כהנא showed. In this version the post was the reverse: seen from outside, smooth inside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here, standing inside, you could not see any post. But from outside a piece stuck out. This version still says the post counts, and the next step will give a source for it.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two versions. Version one: post visible inside, flush outside. Version two: post visible outside, flush inside. Both reach the same result: the סוכה is כשרה.

phrases.english: Alternatively,
it was visible from the outside and even on the inside.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version of the answer in step 9.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A post must be visible from inside to count.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even a post seen only from outside counts as פצימין.

steps.title: Support from the laws of a לחי in a מבוי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports the second version from a ruling about a לחי in a מבוי: a post seen from outside counts, and לחי works the same as פצימין.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was stated: something that is visible from outside and flush on the inside is treated as a לחי. And a לחי is the same as פצימין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source to show that a post seen only from outside still counts. The source comes from the laws of a מבוי (alleyway) on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מבוי needs a לחי (side post) at its opening to allow carrying. We already know that a wall piece seen from outside and flush inside counts as a לחי. Since לחי and פצימין follow the same rules, such a piece also counts as פצימין for a סוכה.

keyTerms.meaning: as it was stated (citing an earlier teaching)
is judged as; is treated as
a side post at the opening of a מבוי, which allows carrying on שבת

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the laws of מחיצות carry over from one area of הלכה (עירובין) to another (סוכה).

phrases.english: As it was stated: something visible from the outside
and even on the inside is treated as a side post.
phrases.notes: This is said about the opening of a מבוי.

phrases.english: And a side post is the same as posts.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a source for the second version in step 10.
steps.raayaObject: A post visible only from outside counts as פצימין.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ruling in עירובין that such a piece counts as a לחי, together with the idea that לחי and פצימין are the same.
steps.whatToRemember: A post can count even if it shows from only one side. From the inside or from the outside, it works as פצימין, just like a לחי in a מבוי. So רב כהנא's סוכה was כשרה.

steps.title: A ברייתא: roofing that extends beyond the סוכה counts as the סוכה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that פסל sticking out from the סוכה is treated like the סוכה itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: פסל that extends out from the סוכה is treated like the סוכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting a ברייתא. This sets up the next question about what the ברייתא means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: פסל is leftover plant material that can be used as סכך. The ברייתא says that when it sticks out past the סוכה, that part has the same status as the סוכה. The wording is unclear, so the גמרא will ask about it next.

keyTerms.meaning: leftover plant material usable as סכך

phrases.english: It was taught: waste material that extends out from the sukkah
is treated like the sukkah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new topic after the story of רב כהנא ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: פסל that sticks out from the סוכה is treated like the סוכה.

steps.title: What does 'פסל extending from the סוכה' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what case the ברייתא is describing.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is 'פסל that extends out from the סוכה'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a simple question to understand the ברייתא. It wants to know what situation the words describe.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not an attack. The phrase 'extends out from the סוכה' could mean several things, so the גמרא asks for the exact case.

phrases.english: What is waste material that extends out from the sukkah?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the meaning of the ברייתא in step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What case the phrase 'פסל היוצא מן הסוכה' describes.

steps.title: עולא: branches sticking out behind the סוכה
steps.stepSummary: עולא explains that the ברייתא means סכך branches that stick out past the back wall of the סוכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: these are branches that stick out behind the סוכה.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא answers the question. The ברייתא means סכך that runs past the back wall of the סוכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The סכך does not stop at the back wall but keeps going outside it. The ברייתא says the area under that extra סכך counts as part of the סוכה. The גמרא will soon examine how this works, since that area is not clearly enclosed by walls.

keyTerms.meaning: behind the סוכה, past its back wall

phrases.english: Ulla said:
Branches that extend out behind the sukkah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא means סכך branches that stick out past the back wall of the סוכה.

steps.title: Doesn't the extra area need three walls?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges עולא: a סוכה needs three walls, so how can the outer area count?
steps.simpleTranslation: But we need three walls!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges עולא's explanation. The area behind the סוכה only has branches over it, so where are its three walls?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every valid סוכה needs at least three walls (שלש דפנות). If the outer section has no walls of its own, it should not count as a סוכה at all. This is the first of three checks on עולא's case.

keyTerms.meaning: But don't we need (opens a challenge)
Three walls, the minimum walls for a סוכה

phrases.english: But don't we need three walls!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges עולא's case from Step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's explanation that the outer branches form a valid area.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A סוכה needs three walls, and the outer area seems to lack them.

steps.title: The case has three walls
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the case is where the outer area does have three walls.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where there are.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that עולא is talking about a case where the outer area really has three walls.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The side walls keep going past the back wall. So the outer area has the two side walls plus the shared back wall, which makes three.

keyTerms.meaning: In a case where it exists (the requirement is met)

phrases.english: Where there are (three walls).
phrases.notes: The side walls extend behind, and the back wall serves both areas.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 15.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The outer area has no walls.
steps.terutzMaskana: The case is where the outer area has three walls.

steps.title: Doesn't the extra area need the minimum size?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges again: a סוכה needs a minimum size.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we need the minimum fitness of a סוכה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second challenge. A סוכה must be at least the minimum size, so is the outer area big enough?
steps.deeperAnalysis: הכשר סוכה here means the smallest size that counts, seven טפחים by seven טפחים. A narrow strip sticking out would be too small.

keyTerms.meaning: The minimum requirements for a valid סוכה (here, its minimum size)

phrases.english: But don't we need the minimum fitness of a sukkah!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge on the same case.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The outer area may be smaller than the minimum size of a סוכה.

steps.title: The case has the minimum size
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the outer area is big enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where there is.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the case is where the outer area is at least the minimum size.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same short answer is used again. The case is narrowed so that this requirement is met.

phrases.english: Where there is (the minimum size).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 17.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The outer area is too small.
steps.terutzMaskana: The case is where it is at least seven by seven טפחים.

steps.title: Doesn't the extra area need more shade than sun?
steps.stepSummary: A third challenge: the סכך must give more shade than sun.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we need its shade to be more than its sun!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third challenge. Branches sticking out may be thin, so do they give more shade than sun?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A valid סוכה needs צלתה מרובה מחמתה, meaning more shade than sunlight. Loose branches that stick out might not meet this rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Its shade is more than its sunlight

phrases.english: But don't we need its shade to be more than its sun!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third challenge on the same case.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Branches sticking out may let in more sun than shade.

steps.title: The case has more shade than sun
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the outer branches do give more shade than sun.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where there is.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the case is where the outer area has more shade than sun.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now all three basic requirements are met in the outer area: walls, size, and shade. This sets up the next question.

phrases.english: Where there is (more shade than sun).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 19.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The outer area has too much sun.
steps.terutzMaskana: The case is where shade is more than sun.

steps.title: If so, what is the ברייתא teaching?
steps.stepSummary: If the outer area has everything a סוכה needs, it is obviously valid. So why state it?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why say it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks: if the outer area meets every rule, it is simply a normal סוכה, so what new point does the ברייתא make?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The three answers made the case so complete that the ruling now seems obvious. A ruling that teaches nothing new is hard to accept, so the גמרא asks for its new point.

phrases.english: If so, what is there to say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the three answers: now the ruling seems obvious.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for the ברייתא's ruling according to עולא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If all requirements are met, the ruling teaches nothing new.

steps.title: The walls count even though they were built for the inside
steps.stepSummary: The new point: we might think the walls only serve the original inner סוכה. The ברייתא teaches that they also count for the outer area.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might say: since the walls were made for the inside and not for the outside, say no. It teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the new point. The walls were originally put up for the inner סוכה, and the ברייתא teaches that they still count for the outer area.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The back wall was clearly built to close off the inner סוכה, so we might think it does not 'belong' to the outer area. The ברייתא teaches that what matters is the walls that are there, not the purpose they were built for.
steps.whatToRemember: According to עולא, the outer area is a full סוכה. The new point is that walls built for the inner סוכה also count for it.

phrases.english: You might have said:
since they were made for the inside
and were not made for the outside —
say no (it does not count); it teaches us (that it does).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 21 by giving the new point.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Walls built for the inner סוכה do not count for the outer area.
steps.terutzMaskana: They do count. What matters is the walls that are there, not why they were built.

steps.title: רבה and רב יוסף: branches sticking out in front
steps.stepSummary: A different case: branches stick out from the open front of the סוכה, and one wall continues along with them. The outer part counts as part of the סוכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה and רב יוסף both say: here it is about branches sticking out in front of the סוכה, and one wall runs along with them. You might say this part lacks the minimum of a סוכה. It teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה and רב יוסף give their own answer to the question of what case the ברייתא means. This is an alternative to עולא's case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In their case, the part sticking out has only one wall and could not stand alone as a סוכה. The ברייתא teaches that it is still valid, because it is an extension of the main סוכה. It is unlike עולא's case, where the outer area was a full סוכה by itself.

keyTerms.meaning: In front of the סוכה (past the open entrance side)

steps.confusionAlert: Here לפנים means 'in front of' the סוכה, not 'inside' it. The branches stick out past the open entrance.

phrases.english: Rabbah and Rav Yosef both say:

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא בְּקָנִים הַיּוֹצְאִים לִפְנִים מִן הַסּוּכָּה,
phrases.english: Here it is about reeds that stick out in front of the sukkah,
and one wall continues along with them.

phrases.aramaic: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא: הָא לֵית בַּהּ הֶכְשֵׁר סוּכָּה,
phrases.english: You might have said: this does not have the minimum fitness of a sukkah,
it teaches us (that it is valid).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the question of Step 13 and gives a different answer than עולא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What case the ברייתא is describing (from Step 13).
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Branches stick out in front of the סוכה with one wall continuing along. They are valid as an extension of the סוכה, even though they lack the minimum on their own.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a part of the סוכה which could not stand alone can still be valid by being attached to a valid סוכה.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: a small part with too much sun
steps.stepSummary: A third case: one סוכה where most of it has more shade than sun, and a small part has more sun than shade. The small part does not make the whole סוכה invalid.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: it is needed only for a סוכה where most of it has more shade than sun, and a small part has more sun than shade. You might say it becomes invalid because of that small part. It teaches us that it does not.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר בר חנה, quoting רבי יוחנן, gives another case for the ברייתא. This is a third alternative explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here nothing physically sticks out. The question is whether a small sunny part ruins the whole סוכה. The ברייתא teaches that the small part is treated as part of the valid סוכה, so the whole סוכה stays valid.

keyTerms.meaning: It was needed only for (this case)

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbah bar bar Chana said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
It was needed only for a sukkah
where in most of it, its shade is more than its sun,
and in a small part of it, its sun is more than its shade.
You might have said: it becomes invalid because of that little part,
it teaches us (that it does not).

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: לֹא נִצְרְכָה אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another answer to Step 13, different from both עולא and רבה with רב יוסף.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What case the ברייתא is describing.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A סוכה with a small part that has more sun than shade. The small part does not make the whole סוכה invalid.

steps.title: Then what does 'sticking out' mean?
steps.stepSummary: On רבי יוחנן's reading nothing physically sticks out, so the גמרא asks what the word יוצא means.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is 'sticking out'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how רבי יוחנן reads the word יוצא in the ברייתא. In his case nothing extends out of the סוכה. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא speaks of פסל היוצא, meaning פסל that sticks out. Since רבי יוחנן's case has no physical extension, the word needs a new meaning.

phrases.english: And what does 'sticking out' mean?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how the ברייתא's wording fits רבי יוחנן's case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of יוצא according to רבי יוחנן.

steps.title: It sticks out of the rules, not out of the building
steps.stepSummary: יוצא means that part of the סוכה goes outside the rules for a valid סוכה, because there it has more sun than shade.
steps.simpleTranslation: It sticks out of the fitness of a סוכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that 'sticking out' means sticking out of הכשר סוכה, the rules for a valid סוכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sunny part 'sticks out' because it does not meet the rule of more shade than sun. It is not about anything physically going beyond the walls, so the wording fits רבי יוחנן's case.

keyTerms.meaning: Goes outside the rules for a valid סוכה

steps.whatToRemember: So far there are three readings of the ברייתא. עולא: branches behind the back wall form a full second סוכה. רבה and רב יוסף: branches in front, with one wall, count as an extension. רבי יוחנן: a small sunny part does not make the whole סוכה invalid. A fourth reading, from רבי אושעיא, comes in the next step.

phrases.english: It sticks out of the fitness of a sukkah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: יוצא means going outside the rules of a valid סוכה, not a physical extension.

steps.title: רבי אושעיא: the ברייתא is about a small strip of unfit roofing in a small סוכה
steps.stepSummary: רבי אושעיא offers another way to read the ברייתא. It teaches that סכך פסול less than three טפחים wide in a סוכה קטנה does not make the סוכה invalid. Here, יוצא means 'goes outside the rules of a סוכה.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אושעיא said: The ברייתא is only needed for unfit roofing that is less than three handbreadths wide, in a small סוכה. And what does 'יוצא' mean? It means that strip goes outside the status of a valid סוכה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new אמורא, רבי אושעיא, gives his own explanation of the ברייתא. He says it is talking about a narrow strip of unfit roofing in a small סוכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like רבי יוחנן's reading, nothing physically sticks out of the סוכה here. So רבי אושעיא also reads יוצא as 'leaves the rules of a סוכה': the strip is made of unfit material. Even so, the ברייתא teaches that the strip does not ruin the whole סוכה.

keyTerms.meaning: Unfit roofing, material that may not be used as סוכה covering
A small סוכה, just about the minimum size of seven by seven טפחים
It was only needed for, introducing the specific case a source teaches
The status or rules of a valid סוכה

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up רבי אושעיא (here) with רב הושעיא (next step). They are two different אמוראים, and the second one challenges the first.

phrases.english: Rabbi Oshaya said:
It was needed only for
unfit roofing less than three handbreadths,
in a small sukkah.
And what does 'extends' mean?
It goes out of the status of a sukkah.
phrases.notes: Not a physical sticking out. The strip is outside the rules because the material is unfit.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא אָמַר: לֹא נִצְרְכָה אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another explanation of the ברייתא, alongside רבי יוחנן's sun-and-shade reading, and reuses the same non-physical meaning of יוצא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What case is the ברייתא coming to teach?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A strip of unfit roofing less than three טפחים wide in a small סוכה; it does not make the סוכה invalid.

steps.title: רב הושעיא objects: unfit roofing is surely no worse than empty air
steps.stepSummary: רב הושעיא challenges רבי אושעיא. Even an empty gap of air under three טפחים does not invalidate a small סוכה. Unfit roofing is surely no worse than air, so the ברייתא would be teaching nothing new.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הושעיא objected: Let the unfit roofing be no worse than empty air. And does a gap of air less than three handbreadths in a small סוכה make it invalid? Of course not!
steps.whatsHappening: רב הושעיא attacks רבי אושעיא's reading. He argues that it makes the ברייתא say something too obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An open gap under three טפחים is treated as closed (לבוד), so it does not ruin a small סוכה. If empty air does not invalidate, unfit roofing in the same spot surely does not. So why would the ברייתא need to teach it?

keyTerms.meaning: Let it be no worse than, a comparison used to show a case is obvious
Empty air, an open gap in the roofing

phrases.english: Rav Hoshaya objected to it:
Let it be no worse than empty air,
and does air less than three handbreadths
in a small sukkah make it invalid?
phrases.notes: A rhetorical question. The answer is no, because of לבוד.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי אושעיא's explanation as making the ברייתא teach nothing new.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אושעיא's reading of the ברייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Unfit roofing cannot be worse than empty air, and air under three טפחים does not invalidate. So the ruling is obvious and the ברייתא would be pointless.

steps.title: רבי אבא: unfit roofing is better than air because you may sleep under it
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא answers that there is a difference. Both the unfit roofing and the small air gap count toward the size of the סוכה. But under unfit roofing you may even sleep, while under the air gap you may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא said to him: This one (unfit roofing) joins in, and people may sleep under it. That one (air) joins in, but people may not sleep under it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא defends רבי אושעיא by showing that the ברייתא does teach something new about unfit roofing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A small air gap only helps the סוכה reach its minimum size; the spot under it is still not a place to sit or sleep. A small strip of unfit roofing is swallowed up into the valid roofing, so a person may even sleep under it. That extra point is what the ברייתא adds.

keyTerms.meaning: Combines or joins in, counting toward the required size

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up two levels: something can count toward the size of the סוכה without being a valid place to sit or sleep. The next question builds on that idea.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba said to him:
This one combines, and one may sleep under it,
and that one combines, but one may not sleep under it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב הושעיא's objection by drawing a difference between unfit roofing and air.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Unfit roofing and empty air are equal, so the ברייתא teaches nothing.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both count toward the size, but only unfit roofing may be slept under, so the ברייתא teaches that extra point.

steps.title: How can something help the סוכה count when it is not valid itself?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions רבי אבא's idea about air. How can a gap of air count toward the size of the סוכה while the spot under it is not valid to sleep in?
steps.simpleTranslation: Is there anything that joins in to make something count, while it itself is not valid?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the idea that air can count toward the סוכה's size while still not being a valid spot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, if something helps make the סוכה valid, you would expect it to be valid itself. רבי אבא said air under three טפחים counts toward the size but cannot be slept under. The גמרא asks whether such a split status exists anywhere in הלכה.

keyTerms.meaning: Is there anything at all?, introducing a skeptical question

phrases.english: And is there anything
that joins in to make up the measure
while it itself is not valid?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the logic behind רבי אבא's distinction.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אבא's claim that air combines but cannot be slept under
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It seems strange for something to help make the סוכה valid while it is not valid itself.

steps.title: רבי יצחק בן אלישיב begins: yes, such a thing exists
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק בן אלישיב answers 'yes': there are things that count toward a measure without being valid themselves. His example continues in the next section.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק בן אלישיב said: Yes,
steps.whatsHappening: This line opens the answer to the question. The גמרא is setting up the next move, where רבי יצחק בן אלישיב will bring an example.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By saying 'yes,' he confirms that this split status exists in halacha. That defends רבי אבא's distinction. The proof itself comes in the next lines.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak ben Elyashiv said:
Yes,
phrases.notes: The answer continues on the next amud with an example.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק בֶּן אֶלְיָשִׁב: אִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question of step 30.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Affirming the premise, with a proof to follow
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Nothing can count toward a measure unless it is valid itself.
steps.terutzMaskana: Such cases do exist, so רבי אבא's distinction stands. The example follows.
